author: claude (direction approved by Desmic, 1 Oct 2026)
learning_promise: An engine reads pieces, not letters or whole words, and its room is counted in pieces.
decisions: Splits are simplified and consistent, made for the game: common words are one piece; rare, long or made-up words split into familiar parts. Real tokenizer splits are explained later (a later level or a side quest).
Room (a fixed number of slots, counted in pieces) is part of Stop 2: it is where the idea pays off, because a message short in letters can still be too long in pieces.
Sources are free to read; see sources.

split_rule.summary: One piece per common word. A rare, long or made-up word splits into a front part, a middle part and an ending, each a piece.
split_rule.why_simplified: Real splits are irregular (they depend on spaces, capitals and training data) and hard to read on a phone. The simplified rule keeps the true idea: frequent strings are single pieces, rare strings cost more pieces.
split_rule.honesty_card: Real engines learn their pieces from huge amounts of text, so their splits look odd (spaces and capitals count). Common words are usually one piece; rare words become several. Room is counted in those pieces.

outcomes.observable_capability: Predict which words in a short message are one piece and which split into several.
outcomes.misconception: The engine reads letters, or it reads whole words.
outcomes.success_evidence: Commit a piece-count prediction for a message before the loom reveals its split; first choice recorded apart from retries.

outcomes.observable_capability: Build a message that fits the engine's room by counting pieces, keeping what matters.
outcomes.misconception: Fewer letters means it fits better; or, if a message is too long, the end is cut off harmlessly.
outcomes.success_evidence: Build a call from word tiles (do what, who, from what) whose split is only shown when it weaves; the first weave is recorded apart from retries, with whether it fit and whether a letter-short, piece-long word was chosen.

sequence.player_goal: Weave the short call 'Free Tavi now'.
sequence.decision: None assessed: Zip lifts each piece onto the rail and the loom counts slots (3 of 6).
sequence.feedback: Every common word fills one slot; the band weaves a little.

sequence.player_goal: The Warden's long message jams the loom. Predict how many slots it needs.
sequence.decision: predict-pieces: pick a number of pieces before the loom splits the message.
sequence.feedback: The rare word splits into three coloured pieces on the rail; the count shows where the prediction was off.
sequence.assistance: A wrong prediction can happen; the split is shown afterwards and the next try is not first.

sequence.player_goal: Weave your own call to free Tavi from word tiles: do what, who, from what. It must fit six slots.
sequence.decision: build-call: tiles go on the rail as whole words; the loom splits them only when it weaves. The tempting verbs (Unhex, Disenchant) are short in letters and long in pieces; four calls fit exactly (Free/Release + Tavi/the weaver + from the loom).
sequence.feedback: The letter-short message overflows: its last pieces fall off the rail and the needed name is lost. The common-word message fits and Tavi is freed.
sequence.assistance: The tempting wrong choice is allowed; recovery is a retry with the split visible.
sequence.completion_evidence: First choice logged; finishing alone is not mastery.
sequence.changed: 30 Oct 2026, after blind run 29 ('picking from 3 or 4 buttons… a bit guessable'; wanted to build something): was a choice between two given calls.
